title: Reading at the end of the input
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with registers $rho$ and labels $Lambda$. If the instruction at label $ell$ reads the next input bit and the input has no bit at position $p$, then from any output string $o$, the program reaches label $ell_e$ within one step, leaving the registers, input position, and output unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $ell$ is a read instruction with end label $ell_e$
The input has no bit at position $p$
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$ and $\ell$ a label whose
instruction is $\mathsf{rd}(\ell_e, \ell_0, \ell_1)$, ``read the next input
symbol and go to $\ell_e$, $\ell_0$ or $\ell_1$ according as the input has ended,
the symbol is $0$, or it is $1$''.  If $x$ has no symbol at (zero-based) position
$p$, i.e.\ $p \ge |x|$, then for all registers $\rho$, from label $\ell$ with
registers $\rho$ and $p$ symbols read the program reaches label $\ell_e$ with
registers $\rho$ and still $p$ symbols read within one step, printing nothing.
